analysis.title: Build resilience as tech volatility rises (UBS House View - Daily US)
key_insights: Tech earnings raised fresh concerns about AI capital expenditure and weaker core-business growth at megacap tech. Nasdaq futures pointed about 2% lower ahead of the US open on Friday, and stocks in Japan, South Korea and Taiwan fell after the Wall Street tech selloff.
Signs that the US may resume military strikes against Iran pushed oil higher, with Brent around USD 117/bbl at the time of writing.
UBS says retreating from markets is not an effective way to protect against drawdowns. It sees scope for equity gains overall and recommends building a resilient portfolio with exposure beyond tech.

UBS sees AI demand as robust but flags a rising risk of mid-cycle capex indigestion. The funding mix for AI investment is shifting from hyperscaler cash flows toward debt, equity, leases and supplier-backed financing.

Accelerating cloud revenue growth and expanding advanced orders for cloud computing capacity point to still-robust AI infrastructure demand, but financing and execution risks are emerging in the more capital-intensive parts of the buildout.
US Q3 GDP grew at a 3.4% annualized rate versus the 3.1% estimate and 2.2% in Q2. The growth has kept inflation elevated and supports sectors beyond tech.

The equal-weighted S&P 500 has outperformed the market-cap-weighted index year to date, which UBS reads as support from cyclical improvement, healthy consumer spending and structural themes such as the longevity industry.

The 10-year US Treasury yield fell 37 basis points in October as equities came under pressure. UBS says quality bonds are acting as a portfolio stabilizer and that elevated yields compensate for yield-volatility risk.

Within tech, UBS likes leading megacaps, defensive payment networks and consumer electronics names, and quality semis and hardware. Investors with outsized US tech allocations should diversify across sectors and regions. Those who can tolerate the risks can consider broad commodities and hedge funds.
The ECB held rates unchanged as expected and warned that inflation risks are tilted to the upside as oil and gas prices rise. Lagarde said she will leave office on 7 February 2027.

UBS considers the 75 basis points of additional ECB tightening priced by markets excessive and expects European borrowing costs to fall into next year. It sees selective opportunities to add duration in high-quality European bonds, favoring short- to medium-term maturities. French fiscal and political risks could keep sovereign spreads volatile.
UBS expects EURUSD to recover toward 1.16 by year-end and says Lagarde's departure does not change that base case.

The BoJ held its policy rate at 1.25% in an 8-to-1 vote, in line with consensus. It judged underlying inflation to be generally consistent with the 2% target for the first time and raised its FY2027 inflation forecast by 20 basis points to 2.6%.

The BoJ accelerated planned ETF sales to JPY 860bn a year (USD 5.47bn) from January 2027, up from JPY 330bn. UBS says this is about 0.1% of market trading volume and expects share buybacks to absorb it.

UBS keeps its forecast of two more 25 basis point BoJ hikes to a terminal rate of 1.75%. It keeps USDJPY forecasts at 160 for December 2026 and 158 thereafter and would not chase near-term yen gains. A terminal rate above 2% is the main downside risk to USDJPY.
UBS remains constructive on Japanese equities, citing AI-related capital spending, cyclical improvement and corporate reform.

Constructive on AI-related capital spending, cyclical improvement and continued corporate reform, with buybacks expected to absorb BoJ ETF sales.
Bonds rallied as equities fell, and elevated yields provide enough income to offset yield-volatility risk.
Resilient 3.4% Q3 growth, an improving cyclical backdrop and healthy consumer spending support sectors outside tech.

Cloud revenue growth is accelerating and advanced orders for cloud computing capacity are expanding, per latest results cited by UBS.
Robust earnings growth across the Eurozone and Asia is cited as widening the opportunity set.
Apple earnings are on the watch list for 2 November.
